why: Sort indices to keep original positions: instead of sorting the values (and losing where they were), sort the list 0..n-1 by the key (-nums[i], i), which gives the rank order and the tie rule at once.
hints: If you sort nums itself, where did the 4th largest value come from? You need the positions to survive the sort.
Sort the indices, not the values. What key makes larger values come first and, among equals, smaller indices first?
order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (-nums[i], i)); return order[k-1]. O(n log n); quickselect or a heap of size k are follow-ups.
pitfalls: Equal values occupy separate ranks, smaller original index first.
